# openehr-assets

Regenerates the files committed under [`assets/`](../assets), and fails the
build if what is committed does not match.

Not published. This is a repository tool, not part of the library's surface.

## Why generated files are committed at all

A diff is the cheapest review there is, and this repository's recurring defect
is a change whose consequences nobody saw.

The schema is declared once, in Rust (`db:G2.7`), and each of the six dialect
crates renders it into that engine's SQL. Nothing in a pull request shows what
the *SQL* became — a reviewer would have to run six commands to find out, and
reviewers do not. With the DDL committed, a type mapping that changes shows up
as a changed `.sql` file, and a dialect that becomes a copy of another shows up
as **two identical files side by side**.

That last property is the point. `openehr-mariadb` shipped as a
name-substituted copy of `openehr-mysql`, and the one thing that would have
caught it at review time was seeing the two generated scripts next to each
other (`spec/audit.md` **W-01**).

## What it generates

| File | Is |
| --- | --- |
| `schema.json` | the shared five-table schema, as data |
| `ddl/<engine>.sql` | that schema rendered by each dialect — one file per engine |
| `column-type-matrix.md` | every logical `ColTy` as all six engines spell it, side by side |
| `invariant-coverage.md` | which of RM 1.1.0's 155 invariants the `openehr` crate cites, matched by scanning the source for `(class, invariant)` literal pairs — not by trusting a hand-maintained list |

Nine files in total. Full description of each, and what
`invariant-coverage.md` does and does not prove, in
[`assets/README.md`](../assets/README.md) — that file documents the *output*;
this one documents the *tool*.

Two more files live in `assets/` but are **not** generated by this crate:
`rm-1.1.0-invariants.json` and `rm-1.1.0-attributes.json` are vendored inputs,
distilled from the openEHR BMM. `check` does not police them, because nothing
here derives them from anything.

## Commands

```sh
cargo run             # same as `write`
cargo run -- write    # regenerate every file under assets/
cargo run -- check    # fail, naming the stale files, if committed != regenerated
```

`check` is the half that matters. Regeneration nobody verifies is regeneration
that quietly stops happening — a schema change lands, `assets/` is not
updated, and the tree carries a lie until someone notices. `check` is what CI
runs on every push (the `assets` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so that
failure mode is a red CI check instead.

## The invariant scanner is the part most likely to be wrong quietly

`invariant_coverage` decides whether the crate cites `("CLASS",
"Invariant_name")` by scanning the source text for two adjacent string
literals that look like a class name and an identifier, separated only by a
comma — not by matching a hard-coded list of call forms. That generality is
deliberate (`lib:A-25`: an earlier version matched specific function-call
shapes and missed every invariant enforced through a shared helper), but a
scanner that matches on *shape* rather than *meaning* can also match shapes
that are not citations at all — a table of test expectations, for instance
(`lib:A-31`). `src/main.rs`'s own test module exercises both directions: real
citation forms it must recognise, and adjacent-but-unrelated literals it must
not.

If you change what counts as a citation, add a case to that test module in the
same change. A measuring instrument with no tests measures whatever it happens
to do — this one had three findings in a row (`lib:A-24`, `lib:A-25`, and a
correction to `A-25` itself) before it had any.

## What this is not

Not `db:G2.1`, which required generating DDL **from** an openEHR specification
package, and was withdrawn: openEHR has nothing to generate a schema from
(`db:S1.5`). This tool renders a schema that already exists in Rust code.
Nothing reads these files back — a schema read from JSON at runtime would be a
second source of truth, and the whole point here is that there is one.
